title: Pocket feature axioms — mini-PRD and notes
content:
Context / motivation:
- I want a small, cheap, predictable assistant surface that people can call with one tap from product surfaces (composer, search, docs).
- Focus: ultra-low-friction helper for quick tasks (summarize, next-action, format).
- Constraint: single-token budget per user interaction (configurable), <150ms p95 latency target for perceived instant UX, and tight cost guardrails.

Proposal name: Pocket (working name) — one-tap compact assistant tile with pre-defined behavior modes (Classic, Tight, Explain).
Axioms: short statements that guide design decisions
1) Predictable cost: default mode must have deterministic cost per interaction (no surprise long generations).
2) Bounded context: Pocket uses last N tokens or a lightweight summary of the session; explicit per-call context budget.
3) Single-call surfacing: treat Pocket as a synchronous micro-inference endpoint optimized for short outputs.
4) Fast fallback: if dedicated capacity unavailable, fall back to a lower-fidelity variant with same payload shape.
5) Minimal surface: tiny UI, no modal full chat by default (option to escalate to full chat).

Target personas:
- Power readers: want quick summaries and highlights while reading docs.
- Customer success reps: quick canned responses and TL;DR of threads.
- Engineers: formatting helpers, code extraction, and simple refactors.

Hypotheses to validate:
- H1: Users will prefer a one-tap mini-assistant for quick tasks more than opening full assistant flows.
- H2: Bounded-budget defaults will materially reduce cost without reducing user satisfaction for micro-tasks.
- H3: Offering 3 clear modes (Classic, Tight, Explain) covers 80% of quick use cases.

Modes (initial):
- Classic: conversational-ish, up to 120 tokens output, balanced temperature 0.2, p95 latency target 150ms on hosted.
- Tight: shortest useful answer, up to 40 tokens, deterministic templates, temp 0.0, for copy/format tasks.
- Explain: a single-paragraph reasoning trace, up to 160 tokens, but charged as two units (costly) and gated behind telemetry thresholds.

User stories (examples):
- As a reader, I want a 2-sentence summary of the current article so I can decide to read fully. Acceptance: summary <= 60 tokens, includes 2 bullet takeaways.
- As an agent, I want a suggested next action for an email thread so I can respond faster. Acceptance: 1 short actionable sentence + 1 suggested subject line.
- As a developer, I want to extract the function signature from a code block. Acceptance: returns syntactically valid signature, < 40 tokens.

API sketch (product-facing):
POST /v1/pocket/respond
payload: {"mode": "Classic|Tight|Explain", "prompt_context": "<text>", "context_budget_tokens": 384, "response_token_limit": 120, "client_request_id": "..."}
response: {"answer": "...", "tokens_used": 42, "variant": "gpt-like-quantized-v1"}
Notes: keep shape minimal so UI can render quickly and optionally escalate with the same request id.

Instrumentation / metrics
- PocketInvocationCount, PocketP95Latency_ms, PocketTokensPerInvocation, PocketEscalationRate (to full chat), PocketSatisfaction (NPS prompt inline: thumbs), CostPerThousandCalls.
- Telemetry tag: pocket_mode, routing_variant, fallback_reason, e2e_request_id.

Rollout plan (0->1):
- Week 0: internal dogfood in Docs app, QA on latency and cost accounting.
- Week 1: beta to 5% of new users in a single product surface (Docs reading).
- Week 2-3: expand to 20%, collect qualitative feedback & telemetry.
- Week 4: iterate modes, add per-user opt-out, soft launch.

A/B experiment ideas:
- Control: no Pocket tile. Variant A: Classic default. Variant B: Tight default. Compare invocation rate, mean session length change, and cost delta.

Fallback & safety considerations:
- If runtime selects fallback model variant due to capacity, return a short apology + minimal answer and increment PocketEscalationRate.
- For PII detection: run a lightweight redaction heuristic before sending context to hosted API; if flagged, show escalation to secure Private deployment flow (enterprise).

Dependencies / engineering notes:
- Need a lightweight endpoint in serving-runtime optimized for short outputs (fast kernel selection, pre-warmed micro-batches).
- Console: new per-route metric dashboard + token-cost breakdown for Pocket.
- SDK: tiny helper in web SDK to render tile and manage escalation flow.
- Routing/policy: TTL-based prefix caching to reuse recent summaries.

Risks / unknowns:
- Perceived slowness: 150ms p95 is optimistic; might need dedicated micro-instances.
- Cost leakage from repeated rapid invocations. Mitigations: client-side debounce, server-side rate limiting and credits.
- Mode confusion: users might expect full chat; need clear affordance for escalation.

Open questions / decisions:
- Default token cap per account vs global default? (pro: fairness; con: overhead).
- Metrics to gate Explain mode — should it be gated by a usage quota?
- Should Pocket persist a micro-history per user (stitching across pages) or be stateless per surface?

Next concrete tasks (for next sync):
1) Ask SRE: estimated cost and latency for 500 qps micro-endpoint. (owner: Ravi)
2) Prototype web tile and debounce behavior (owner: Jillian).
3) Small UX test with 8 dogfooders to validate reaction time and perceived utility (owner: Priya).
4) Draft JIRA epic + acceptance criteria for engineering (linked: JIRA-INF-789).

Notes to self (scratch):
- Could reuse compact-response-allocator heuristics to pick model variant.
- Consider low-cost quantized model for Tight mode to save budget.
- Keep the UI copy extremely explicit: "Pocket: quick help — tap for 2-line summary"

Fragments for copy:
- "Quick summary" / "One-line action" / "Explain this in plain words"
- CTA: "Open full assistant" (escalate)

End of draft.
